As pointed out in Seber and Wild (1989), there exist two different parameterisations of the Weibull model. They do not yield the same fitted curve for a given dataset (see under Examples).

The four-parameter Weibull type 1 model ('weibull1') is

f(x)=c+(d−c)exp(−exp(b(log(x)−log(e)))).

The four-parameter Weibull type 2 model ('weibull2') is

f(x)=c+(d−c)(1−exp(−exp(b(log(x)−log(e))))).

Both four-parameter model functions are asymmetric with inflection point at the dose equal e

The three-parameter Weibull type 1 model is given by the expression

f(x)=0+(d−0)exp(−exp(b(log(x)−log(e)))).

The model function is asymmetric about the inflection point, which is the parameter 
exp(e).

The three-parameter Weibull type 1 model with upper limit 1 is given by the expression

f(x)=0+(1−0)exp(−exp(b(log(x)−log(e)))).
